title: Throughput Sentinel: traffic-sliced batching advisor with adaptive throttles and automated revert
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We want automated batching and KV-caching recommendations that reduce token cost without violating latency/throughput SLOs. Current manual tuning and blunt canaries risk wide regression windows or overly conservative settings that leave cost on the table.

Goal: Build a production-safe system (Throughput Sentinel) that proposes and applies staged batching/cache changes per-traffic-slice, enforces adaptive limiters, watches SLO signals and anomalies, and automatically reverts bad changes. Deliver a recommendation engine, a staged-apply pipeline, an anomaly detector tuned for latency/throughput, and operator UX for overrides/observability.

Success metrics:
- median token cost reduction across staging customers >= 12% within first month of rollout
- zero P1 incidents caused by automated applies during beta
- < 1% of applies requiring manual rollback after automated revert triggers
- no more than 5% increase in p99 latency for targeted slices while maintaining throughput targets

Scope:
- Recommendation generator: offline profiler + online telemetry to produce per-route batching/window and KV cache hints.
- Staged apply orchestrator: apply changes to tiny traffic slices first (shadow & canary), measure, then incrementally enlarge slice with automatic gating.
- Adaptive throttles: runtime limiters that temporarily reduce batching window or divert traffic to lower-cost models if SLOs degrade.
- Anomaly detector: hybrid rules + statistical change detection on latency percentiles, error rates, and throughput drop. Tuned for low false positives and bounded detection latency.
- Automated revert: deterministic rollback policy triggered when SLO breach or anomaly persists beyond grace window. Detailed logging and rollback reason metadata.

Non-goals: fully autonomous tuning without human review for high-sensitivity routes; replacing existing manual rollout system entirely in first phase.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Traffic slicing granularity: choose route + customer_id hash slice to isolate noisy tenants. Trade-off: finer slices reduce blast radius but slow learning. We'll start with 1% -> 5% -> 20% progression per route.
- Detection sensitivity: prefer slightly conservative thresholds (higher specificity) to avoid costly false reverts; combine with multi-metric gating to reduce spurious triggers.
- Revert policy: automated revert after 3 consecutive detection windows (configurable). Human-in-the-loop for repeated flapping.

Monitoring & dashboards: new per-apply dashboard showing cost delta, p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, tokens/sec, and detector logs. Integrate with Console rollout traces and alerts to PagerDuty for high-severity regressions.

Security & compliance: does not introduce new customer data paths. All telemetry stays in existing observability pipeline. No secret changes required.

Release plan:
- Phase 0 (MVP): recommendation engine + offline simulation + shadow apply for 1 route (2 weeks)
- Phase 1: staged apply orchestration + basic anomaly detector + manual approve (3 weeks)
- Phase 2: adaptive throttles + automated revert enabled for beta tenants (4 weeks)
acceptance_criteria: Recommendations generated for >= 80% of sampled routes during offline simulation
Staged apply can be executed and rolled back via orchestration API and Console UI
Detector correctly flags injected latency regressions in synthetic tests with >= 90% recall and < 5% false positive rate
Automated revert triggers for a sustained SLO breach and restores previous config within 30s
New dashboard displays apply history, metrics deltas, and detector rationale
